dashboard.title: MySQL
dashboard.description: Monitor a MySQL or MariaDB server: lock contention, temporary tables, thread saturation, InnoDB buffer pool health, and row throughput.

visuals.title: Row lock waits
visuals.description: Times InnoDB had to wait for a row lock. Sustained waits mean transactions are contending for the same rows, usually from long-running transactions or a hot counter row that every request updates.

visuals.title: Row lock wait time
visuals.description: Total time spent waiting for row locks. Read together with row lock waits: a small number of waits with a large wait time points at one slow transaction holding locks rather than broad contention.

visuals.title: Table locks
visuals.description: Table locks acquired immediately versus those that had to wait. A rising share of waited locks means queries are queueing behind each other for table access.

visuals.title: Temporary resources created
visuals.description: Temporary tables and files created while running queries. Temporary tables spilling to disk (disk_tables) are far slower than in-memory ones and usually indicate queries that sort or group without a usable index.

visuals.title: Threads
visuals.description: MySQL thread states. Connected threads approaching max_connections is what produces connection errors in the application; running threads staying high means queries are piling up rather than completing.

visuals.title: Buffer pool usage
visuals.description: Bytes held in the InnoDB buffer pool, split into clean and dirty pages, against the configured pool size. A pool that is permanently full while reads keep hitting disk means innodb_buffer_pool_size is too small for the working set.

visuals.title: Buffer pool operations
visuals.description: Operations against the InnoDB buffer pool. Compare reads (served from disk) against read_requests (served from memory): a growing ratio of reads to read_requests is a falling cache hit rate.

visuals.title: Buffer pool pages
visuals.description: Pages in the InnoDB buffer pool by kind. Free pages trending to zero means the pool is fully committed and InnoDB must evict a page for every new read.

visuals.title: Row operations
visuals.description: InnoDB rows read, inserted, updated and deleted. A read count far larger than the others is the signature of queries scanning many rows to return few.

visuals.title: Handler requests
visuals.description: Requests to MySQL's storage engine handlers. A high read_rnd_next count means full table scans; a high read_key count means queries are using indexes as intended.

visuals.title: InnoDB I/O operations
visuals.description: Reads, writes and fsyncs performed by InnoDB. A climbing fsync rate alongside flat throughput usually means the redo log or the flush settings are the bottleneck rather than the queries.

visuals.title: Log operations
visuals.description: InnoDB redo log activity. Log waits above zero mean the log buffer is too small and transactions are stalling while it is flushed.

visuals.title: Sorts
visuals.description: Sort operations performed. A high merge_passes count means sorts are spilling out of sort_buffer_size and completing on disk.

visuals.title: Opened resources
visuals.description: Files, tables and table definitions opened. A high rate of opened tables against a stable schema means table_open_cache is too small and MySQL is reopening the same tables repeatedly.

visuals.title: Uptime
visuals.description: Seconds since the server started. A reset to zero marks a restart, which also explains any counter on this dashboard dropping back to its starting value.
